subtopics.title: Policy Overview and Targets
subtopics.summary: Delhi EV Policy 2.0 was notified by the Government of NCT of Delhi and is scheduled to come into force from 1 July 2026, remaining effective until 31 March 2030. It builds upon the achievements of Delhi EV Policy 2020 and aims to turn Delhi into a leading electric mobility hub. The policy targets at least 30% electrification of Delhi's total vehicle fleet by 31 March 2030, with a focus on high-usage and high-emission transport segments.
facts: Notified by the Government of NCT of Delhi
In force from 1 July 2026
Effective until 31 March 2030
Builds upon the achievements of Delhi EV Policy 2020
Electrification target: at least 30% of Delhi's total vehicle fleet by 31 March 2030
Focus: electrification of high-usage and high-emission transport segments
Priority segments: 2-wheelers, 3-wheelers, commercial goods carriers, school buses, app-based aggregator fleets, government-owned transport fleets
Objective: widespread adoption of zero-emission vehicles
Objective: reduce urban air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions

subtopics.title: Registration Rules and Phase-out
subtopics.summary: New registrations in Delhi move to electric models in stages. From 1 January 2027 only electric 3-wheelers and electric N1 category light commercial trucks can be newly registered, and from 1 April 2028 new 2-wheeler registrations are restricted to electric models. Existing petrol and diesel vehicles may keep operating until the end of their prescribed service life. Schools must also electrify part of their bus fleets.
facts: From 1 January 2027: only electric 3-wheelers and electric N1 category light commercial trucks newly registered

Long-term objective: 30% electrification of school bus fleets by 2030

subtopics.title: Investment, Support and Charging
subtopics.summary: The policy plans total investment of approximately 15,000 crore. Government support is restricted exclusively to battery electric vehicles and not to hybrid vehicles. The plan includes installing over 30,000 public charging stations across Delhi. Financial support and investment is handled by the Delhi Transport Department, and infrastructure development by Delhi Transco Limited.

Key objective: encourage sustainable public and commercial transport

subtopics.title: National Schemes: NEMMP, FAME and PM E-DRIVE
subtopics.summary: Delhi's policy sits within national electric mobility efforts. The National Electric Mobility Mission Plan was launched in 2013, and the government committed to achieve 30% e-mobility by 2030. FAME India, launched by the Ministry of Heavy Industries & Public Enterprises, is part of that mission plan and offers subsidies for several vehicle types. PM E-DRIVE, launched in 2024 with the Ministry of Heavy Industries as nodal ministry, builds on FAME-II and the Electric Mobility Promotion Scheme 2024.

quizzes.passage: The Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi has notified the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy 2.0. The policy is scheduled to come into force from 1 July 2026 and to remain effective until 31 March 2030. It builds upon the achievements of the Delhi EV Policy 2020 and provides a comprehensive roadmap for transforming Delhi into a leading electric mobility hub. A central focus is reducing vehicular emissions by encouraging the electrification of high-usage and high-emission transport segments. The policy names several priority vehicle segments, including two-wheelers, three-wheelers, school buses, app-based aggregator fleets and government-owned transport fleets. The booklet presents the policy's major provisions under a dedicated heading, and these include timelines for vehicle registration. The booklet also outlines the expected benefits of electric vehicles. These include a likely fall in demand for petrol and diesel, the creation of new jobs in the automobile sector, and a reduction in pollution-induced health problems. The policy's provisions cover financial support and investment as well as infrastructure development, and each area is assigned to a separate implementing body.

quizzes.passage: The booklet describes a set of national schemes that support electric vehicles, alongside its coverage of Delhi's own electric vehicle policy. Among these schemes is a broader national mission plan. FAME India is one of the schemes. Its purpose is to give a boost to the development of electric vehicles, and it works through three approaches: establishing charging stations, incentivising buyers and publicising the benefits of electric vehicles. The booklet lists the expected benefits of this push as a fall in the demand for petrol and diesel, the creation of new jobs in the automobile sector, and a reduction in pollution-induced health problems. PM E-DRIVE is the most recent of the schemes described. Its support covers electric buses, e-trucks, e-ambulances and other new emerging EV categories, and it is described as building on earlier efforts. Its objectives and nodal ministry are listed in a separate section of the booklet. Separately, the booklet notes that Delhi EV Policy 2.0 builds upon the achievements of Delhi EV Policy 2020 and is set to remain effective until 31 March 2030. The policy also describes electrification of high-usage and high-emission transport segments as a way to reduce vehicular emissions.
